title: AD enumeration
overview: Separate expected directory inventory from repeated user enumeration by a workstation account.
prerequisites: Know the basics of AD auditing and how to review authorization context.

attack.name: Domain Account
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A workstation actor issuing repeated directory-wide user-listing queries warrants a directory discovery hunt.
evidence: Compare actor, LDAP query class, query scope and client role. Check how often that actor normally queries the directory.
false_positive: Auditors, administrators and inventory jobs can enumerate users legitimately.
tuning: Separate registered inventory jobs and narrow approvals by actor, source and expected scope.
response: Scope the account, verify its authorization and examine accompanying authentication and access activity.
prevention: Audit directory queries for sensitive objects and reduce the reach of unmanaged directory clients.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: Provider-specific query result shape and attribution vary. The dataset supplies aggregate scope rather than raw LDAP filters.

options: Ordinary workstation versus managed inventory source
questions.explanation: Client role can distinguish unscheduled discovery from an approved inventory task.
Query scope determines why the event matters and how to investigate it.
